target_customer: Businesses with existing camera systems (industrial, retail, safety) that want to turn video feeds into automated actions
problem: Existing cameras only record, so people must watch feeds or write custom vision models to detect events such as stalled production, safety violations or waiting customers.
business_model: Hosted video language model API plus a hardware station; the pre-order station was listed at 449 USD per month or 6,499 USD up front
product_category: Computer vision, vision language model inference and video agents

founders.name: Andrey Gizdov
education: Harvard, left a computer vision PhD program
founders.background_notes: YC page lists a dropped out PhD in computer vision at Harvard.

founders.name: Vishal Urlam
founders.background_notes: YC page lists CMU and ECE; the launch post cites embedded systems engineering and camera system automation at Tata.

competitors.name: Visionplatform.ai
competitors.what: Adds reasoning and AI agents to existing camera and VMS deployments for control rooms

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time video language model serving with distillation, hybrid linear attention and quantization is research heavy; the CEO's research was cited as published at CVPR 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Inference speed and custom model building are hard to copy quickly, but open models and many video analytics vendors exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Video analytics vendors and NVIDIA were adding agentic features in 2026; no incumbent action against OpenVector is known.

market_need_then: Large installed base of passive cameras and fast progress in vision language models in 2026 created demand for natural language camera monitoring.

identity.visual_style: technical research style site with benchmark claims

branding.brand_signature: Any camera becomes an autonomous worker
branding.community_and_virality: Founder interview on the Fondo blog; no Product Hunt listing found; a LinkedIn post marked it YC S26.

brand_strength.rationale: Early stage with little press about the brand itself and a generic sounding name that overlaps with many open projects.

outcome_analysis: OpenVector is an Active Summer 2026 company with no outcome yet. Its bet is a technically deep, fast video language model engine from a founder with published vision research, aimed at a large installed base of cameras. Main risks are incumbents in video analytics and open source models narrowing its speed lead. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.
